newsitem.title: USA: Handguns cause disproportionate amount of injuries.
newsitem.headline: Handguns cause disproportionate amount of injuries.

text.p: Handguns make up only half of the new gun sales in the United States but are involved in nearly 90 percent of shootings that result in emergency room visits, according to a new three-city study.
The conclusion is part of a New England Journal of Medicine study that looked at gunshot wounds in Memphis, Tennessee, Galveston, Texas and Seattle between November 1992 and May 1994.
A team led by Dr. Arthur Kellermann said the overwhelming prevalence of handgun injuries was probably caused by "the ability of handguns to be concealed readily and their ease of use."

They also concluded that gun-related injuries "are a major cause" of death and injury in urban areas and that "assaults are the predominant cause of nonfatal gunshot wounds." Nearly 90 percent of the wounds fell in the assault category.

Kellermann and his colleagues reported that the likelihood of being injured by a gun varied from city to city. The annual injury rate was 0.22 percent in Memphis, 0.14 in Galveston and 0.05 percent in Seattle.
